description: The #1 way a latency/throughput load run silently INVALIDATES on this local rig: tracing back-pressure, NOT the app and NOT host CPU. The APISIX opentelemetry plugin is sampler:always_on (one span PER REQUEST, infra/apisix/init-routes.sh:118/:217) and exports SYNCHRONOUSLY through the request-serving nginx worker. Jaeger v2's Badger store accretes (13GB across a multi-week implementation history at 7d TTL); under load its block cache thrashes (hit-ratio 0.03, 1.3M misses), the collector stalls, :4317 refuses connections, and the OTEL export blocks for its 10s retry timeout INSIDE the worker (otlp.lua:48 'Collector retries timed out (timeout 10000)'). Result: 40s tail latencies while the median stays ~6ms, k6's fixed maxVUs=150 pool exhausts waiting on the stalled requests, iterations drop, and run-load.sh REDs the multi-rep run — DETERMINISTICALLY at ~6min in (gate-overhead rep3), reproduced identically at host load-avg 0.7 AND 12. The fingerprint: p50 stays fast, expected_response:true p95 stays fast, but a burst of failures stretches to tens of seconds + thousands of dropped_iterations. Diagnosed by driving the failures to the APISIX error log (the timestamps align exactly to the stall window). Ruled out first: app regression (median rock-steady across reps), desktop CPU (reproduced quiet), token expiry (accessTokenLifespan=1800s), APISIX rate-limiting (no limit-req/limit-count/limit-conn on any route).
resolution: For latency/throughput modes (full/guarded/baseline/ceiling) bring the rig up with ENABLE_TRACING=0 — no OTEL plugin, no Jaeger, no back-pressure path. Proven: the exact rep that collapsed 3 runs straight ran pristine tracing-off, and the ceiling ladder then climbed to a clean app knee. Only the amplification analysis (ADR-0021 6) needs traces, and it runs as its OWN tracing-on pass over a ~500-trace window, separate from the latency numbers. Durable fixes committed (bb21b6b): jaeger-config.yaml span TTL 168h->24h (caps growth); run-load.sh header now documents the ENABLE_TRACING=0 requirement. Operational reset when Badger is already huge: docker volume rm opa-abac-example_jaeger-badger (traces are disposable debug data, never source-of-truth; recreates empty on next tracing-on up). Deeper follow-up (not yet done): a FRACTIONAL OTEL sampler (trace_id_ratio ~0.05) coordinated with the amplification floor logic (offered/2 capped 500) so tracing-on runs keep >=500 traces/scenario without 100% volume.

name: Recorded perf numbers (post-SB4-port): gate +0.79ms p50, ceiling 25rps
description: The recorded post-SB4-port perf numbers (Boot 4.0.7 / Java 25 / Jackson 3, main @ 7cfdb04, PERFORMANCE.md), measured 2026-07-12 telemetry-off on a quiet host, REPS=3 medians, ADR-0021-valid. GATE COST (the headline): the full ABAC gate (subject extraction -> role resolve -> OPA decision) adds +0.79ms (+15%) at p50 vs an identical-gateway unguarded baseline (guarded gate-overhead p50 5.93ms vs baseline 5.14ms), and is statistically FLAT at the tail (p90 +0.01ms, p95 -0.22ms, p99 +0.60ms/+7%). Tightly reproducible (guarded 5.84-5.96, baseline 5.11-5.18). Method: guarded pass, then redeploy ENABLE_OPA=0 (app) while re-wiring the gateway opa plugin back on (init-routes.sh) so the gateway posture is IDENTICAL between passes, then baseline pass; delta = median(guarded p50) - median(baseline p50). LIST CEILING: latency knee at 50 rps, ceiling 25 rps (p99 156ms@10rps -> 170ms@25 -> 5277ms@50; fail 0/0/5.8%). This supersedes the SB4-port's first-pass non-ledger '+1.49ms' figure, which was distorted by the tracing back-pressure. Amplification per-request call bounds (resolve/decide/compile/batch-eval counts) were already validly attributed tracing-on and are byte-identical to the 7.3 contract.

name: Driving run-load.sh: mode map, the identical-gateway two-pass, and reading k6 v2 summaries
description: Operating scripts/load/run-load.sh (the k6 harness) — the non-obvious mechanics that cost time to relearn. MODES: 'guarded' runs gate-overhead+list-filter+enrichment on the current (must-be-guarded) rig AND calls run_amplification on the guarded pass (which REDs 'invalid trace window' if tracing is off/Jaeger empty — but the k6 summary JSONs are written BEFORE the amplification step, line 442 before 450, so the gate-overhead-guarded-repN.summary.json files SURVIVE a post-summary amplification red and can be harvested); 'baseline' runs gate-overhead only, needs the rig redeployed ENABLE_OPA=0 (it ASSERTS the pod flag, does not flip it) AND still needs the gateway opa plugin present (identical-gateway invariant, ADR-0021 2) — a bare ENABLE_OPA=0 deploy strips the gateway plugin, so re-wire with 'ENABLE_OIDC=1 ENABLE_OPA=1 ENABLE_USER_SERVICE=1 bash infra/apisix/init-routes.sh' after the deploy; 'ceiling' is pure latency ladder, NO amplification, NO Jaeger dependency — the cleanest telemetry-free mode; 'full' orchestrates guarded->redeploy->baseline->restore + amplification (so 'full' needs tracing ON for its amplification step). REPS=3 is the official medians. VALIDITY: run-load.sh exits RC=99 and records NOTHING to PERFORMANCE.md when any validity gate trips (ADR-0021 'no invalid number is ever recorded') — a RED run is not a failure to fix, it's the gate working; PERFORMANCE.md staying clean is the proof. Run dirs land in scripts/load/results/<ts>-<mode>/.

name: ADR-0021 load-testing methodology + the scripts/load harness (domain map)
description: Load-testing methodology is pinned in ADR-0021 (docs/architecture/adr/0021-load-testing-methodology.md) and the harness is scripts/load/ (run-load.sh + scenarios/*.js + knee.py + amplification.py). Core tenets: k6 host-run against the REAL rig (gateway->pods->OPA->user-service, never mocks); open-model constant-arrival-rate executors; report-only with VALIDITY-only gates ('no invalid number is ever recorded' — RED on any rig-state/load-error/thin-trace/wrong-fixture failure, never a silently-wrong table row); two-pass gate delta = guarded (app calls OPA) minus baseline (ENABLE_OPA=0) with the GATEWAY posture held identical across passes; the ceiling ladder finds the knee per 5 (p99>1s OR >1% failed/dropped, early-stop); the amplification ratio ( 6) is a guarded-pass-only Jaeger-attributed metric over ~500 traces stating expected-vs-measured per-request downstream call counts (the request-scoped-cache efficiency proof). Fixtures: the reserved dddd... load catalog prefix + the 'perf'/'dora' realm accounts (teardown-on-green). Official numbers live in root PERFORMANCE.md. Predecessor context: the 7.2 LOAD-TESTING slice built the harness; 7.3 RESOLVE-COALESCING re-measured resolve amplification (2/22/102 -> 1/1/1/2); the SB4 port re-baselined once on Boot 4.

name: Measured fault behavior of the rig (T5 baselines)
description: MEASURED (Phase-7.2 T5, three-phase fault timelines at load): (1) a PAUSED OPA fails closed end-to-end as TYPED 403s issued by the APISIX opa plugin after its ~3.0s timeout — no 5xx, no hangs, but every denial costs ~3s (slow-deny finding for 7.3: the gateway plugin timeout budget); (2) the supplier edge under sustained outage (B3 stub down) denies FAST once the resolve breaker opens — deny p50 ~15ms (CallNotPermitted), max ~515ms during initial guard-exhaust; (3) time-to-recovery is breaker-paced: ~8s on the supplier edge (half-open probe lag) vs ~1s on the OPA edge; (4) transient supplier blips are invisible at load (73/74 requests succeed through the guard's retries). Also: k6 constant-arrival-rate fault scenarios need the VU pool FULLY pre-allocated (max(100,RATE*5)) or lazy VU init drops iterations exactly at the fault onset, falsely reddening the dropped_iterations==0 validity gate.

title: Load-testing methodology pinned (ADR 0021): k6 host-run, two-pass ENABLE_OPA=0 baseline, open-model, report-only with validity gates
rationale: Grill-me 2026-07-07 settled all eight Phase-7.2 forks; full rationale in ADR 0021. The non-obvious calls: (1) HOST-installed k6 over containerized — on Docker Desktop a containerized generator competes for the rig's own VM CPU exactly where p99s are read; (2) the unguarded baseline is the EXISTING deploy mechanism (ENABLE_OIDC=1 ENABLE_OPA=0 -> OPA_ABAC_ENABLED=false pods behind the identical gateway) — never a dedicated unguarded endpoint (ships a weakened path to measure a number); (3) open-model constant-arrival-rate because the headline is a p99 delta and closed-model coordinated omission flatters tails; the ceiling scenario is a runner LOOP of 60s constant-rate stages (per-stage summaries + early stop), knee = p99>1s OR >1% fails/dropped-iterations sustained; (4) amplification via the Jaeger API (always_on tracing already in the pods) for ATTRIBUTED per-request outbound counts with expected-vs-measured bounds — counter diffs can't attribute; (5) OPA fault = docker pause (a real hang, the nastier mode) — no toxiproxy for one scenario; (6) report-only + k6 thresholds as VALIDITY-only gates (laptop absolute numbers flake; deltas/ratios/knees are the product; no CI perf runs); (7) the harness's fail-closed analogue is VALIDITY (no invalid number recorded — every failure mode reddens the run) and the restore path IS its fail-open risk (trap-on-exit: rig always ends guarded).

description: MEASURED (Phase-7.2 T4 amplification, Jaeger-attributed, constant across all sampled traces): the library's per-request resolve chatter scales ~1:1 with page rows — a 100-row enriched category page makes 102 identical /internal/effective-role calls (same user, same governing catalog: gate + list-authorizer + one per enriched row via the ActionEnrichmentAdvice path); the 20-row default page makes 22; even a single id'd GET makes 2 (gate + enrichment advice). The request-scoped cache claim pinned in ADR 0021 §6 ('caches bound the chatter: 1 resolve per request') is REFUTED on the resolve edge. The EVAL side is bounded as designed: 2 batch evals per page (one for the page rows + one for the returned envelope), never N×rows.
resolution: 7.3 owns the fix (this slice is report-only): a request-scoped memo on RoleDefinitionSupplier.lookup (keyed user+type+resourceId) would collapse N identical lookups to 1. Numbers + tables live in the T4 amplification results and PERFORMANCE.md; reproduce with scripts/load/run-load.sh guarded (the amplification step runs automatically).

name: Ladder-stage validity split: saturation is data, auth failure is red
description: A load-test ceiling ladder must NOT reuse steady-mode k6 validity thresholds: per ADR 0021 §5 the knee SIGNALS (p99 breach, error rate, dropped iterations) are the measurement, so thresholds on them would abort the run at exactly the point of interest. But dropping all thresholds lets a broken rig (401/403 from a stale realm or missing grant) read as an instant 'errors knee' — a silently wrong number. The split: ladder stages keep ONE threshold, a custom auth_failures Counter (incremented on 401/403) with count==0; everything else is recorded and judged by the offline-testable knee function (knee.py, exit 2 on unreadable summary). Steady scenarios keep the strict trio (http_req_failed rate==0, checks rate==1, dropped_iterations count==0).

name: Load-harness seed: tag-gate the load identity + tag the target to match + canary-probe the chain
description: A k6/load harness measuring the PE list path must bind its load identity to a TAG-GATED read role (ADR 0021 §4: the residual must DISCRIMINATE — an ungated role reduces the category filter residual to allow-all and the ceiling measures nothing), while tagging the load catalog itself with the matching tag so the single-GET scenario stays 200 under the 5.97 attribute-rich gate (a tag-gated role gates the WHOLE decision incl. view). Close the fire-and-forget bootstrap edge (post_json >/dev/null matrix idiom) with a seed-time CANARY PROBE: one gateway GET of the load target as the load identity, 200 or red — a broken token->resolve->decide chain lands red before any measurement window, never as mid-window k6 threshold redness.

name: Bounded gateway-OPA timeout: tune to the LOADED p99; saturation denies become knee data; fleet matrices have per-runner rig postures
description: Three durable operational rules from the 7.3 re-measurement. (1) A gateway OPA-plugin timeout must be tuned against the OPA's LOADED p99, never its idle latency: the sidecar answers idle checks in single-digit ms, but the SAME process serves the app's compile + bulk evals, and under list load its tail crossed 500 ms at just 10 req/s — a 500 ms timeout produced ~2-4% steady-state 403s (apisix 'err: timeout' -> 403); 1000 ms gave zero steady denies while still bounding the outage-deny wall at ~1.0 s vs the 3.0 s default. (2) With a BOUNDED timeout, a saturation-adjacent OPA stall surfaces as a timeout-DENY, so a ceiling ladder must treat 401/403s as knee DATA (the >1%-failed signal), not as broken-rig red — the broken-ACL-chain guard belongs in the seed-time canary probe (which reds before any stage); keep wrong_count==0 as the stage validity gate. (3) The newman fleet is NOT one-rig-fits-all: run-tests + run-matrix are Phase-3 demo-supplier matrices (realm-role creates — on the http role source an unprovisioned editor correctly resolves no role and creates 403); run-team-matrix REQUIRES ENABLE_DIRECTORY=1 (its dora directory-probe preflight); resilience needs the B3 stub rig; spa-smoke needs ENABLE_SPA=1. Each runner documents its posture in its header — read it before batching a fleet. Also: interactive-demo leftovers (teams created via the SPA) contaminate the isolation matrix's membership cut — wipe non-registry demo teams before official fleet runs.

name: Cross-pod concurrency proof: 2 app pods on ONE shared Postgres, contend via the gateway round-robin pool
description: To prove the @Version/mutate() locked-write serialization holds under REAL multi-instance concurrency (not just latch-forced ITs), run the service as 2 pods sharing one DB and drive concurrent conflicting mutations at the SAME row through the APISIX round-robin upstream so they land on different pods. Rig shape (opa-abac usermgmt HA slice): a 2nd container (usermgmt-2:28092) shares usermgmt-postgres with usermgmt-1; the usermgmt-pool APISIX upstream is roundrobin over both host ports; the X-Upstream-Addr response-rewrite header (already wired) shows which pod served each request, so you can PROVE both served. Token: catalog-spa is PKCE-only (directAccessGrantsEnabled=false) → password grant fails 'unauthorized_client'; mint via the CONFIDENTIAL catalog-gateway client (has secret in the realm export) IN-NETWORK (docker exec usermgmt curl keycloak:8888 — issuer must be keycloak:8888). Two tests that exercise the invariant: (1) N concurrent PUT /teams/{t}/members/{u} role-changes on ONE membership alternating two legal roles → assert all 2xx, ZERO 5xx, final state = exactly ONE clean role (no torn/lost update); this mutation is server-serialized (no client 409/If-Match in its OpenAPI). (2) N concurrent ADD(POST)/REMOVE(DELETE) of the same user → assert only legitimate 201/409/204/404 (the DB unique constraint rejects dup inserts across pods, delete is idempotent) and final rows for that user is 0 or 1, NEVER >1 (no double-apply). Result: 24 role-changes → 24×200 both pods, 1 clean role; 20 add/remove → 201/409/204/404, exactly 1 row. Gotcha: the single-member sub-resource is PUT/DELETE-only (no GET → 405); read final state via the members LIST. INV to re-check on any rig LB change: /internal/* still 404 at the edge (never gateway-fronted); the 2nd pod's env must match pod-1 (OPA/ownership/directory) or you get split-brain config. The catalog's internal resolve-read stays pinned to pod-1 (reads identical on shared DB); only the writes spread.

The observability pipeline is a LOAD-BEARING dependency of the rig under list load: with always_on sampling, a 20-row enriched list request emits a ~2,000-span trace (~100 spans/row — span volume amplifies with rows exactly like the resolve calls), so sustained list load OOMs Jaeger v2/Badger; once Jaeger dies, the pods' OTEL export backpressure drags request latency into a death spiral (auth failures from resolve timeouts) even at 5 req/s. Separately, the Jaeger QUERY side dies serving a single /api/traces response of ~150 giant traces (100MB+ payload).
resolution: Official-run protocol (scripts/load/README.md): fresh trace store before official runs (docker compose -f infra/compose.jaeger.yaml down -v). amplification.py fetches in chunked sub-windows (limit 10/slice, dedup by traceID) so giant-trace scenarios stay queryable. run-load.sh carries a universal EXIT heal-trap restarting a dead OPA (the bulk-eval backlog OOMs it at the list collapse point). Production adopters must SAMPLE (always_on is demo-only).

description: ROOT CAUSE of the repeated load-run RC=99 (3 runs, all RED'ing deterministically on gate-overhead rep3 ~6min in) — NOT the app, NOT desktop CPU (reproduced at host load 0.88), NOT token expiry (accessTokenLifespan=1800s), NOT APISIX rate-limiting (no limit-req/limit-count/limit-conn plugin on any route — verified live). IT IS Jaeger/Badger span-storage saturation back-pressuring APISIX's SYNCHRONOUS OTEL exporter. The APISIX opentelemetry plugin is configured sampler:{name:"always_on"} (infra/apisix/init-routes.sh:118 and :217 for user-mgmt) = 100% sampling, one span per request. Under REPS=3 multi-scenario load (tens of thousands of reqs) Jaeger v2's Badger backend (disk volume jaeger-badger:/badger, compose.jaeger.yaml) thrashes — 'Block cache might be too small ... hit-ratio: 0.03', 1.3M cache misses. Badger stalls -> collector :4317 refuses connections -> the APISIX otlp.lua exporter hits its 10s retry timeout ('export_spans(): Collector retries timed out (timeout 10000)') IN ngx.timer context inside the request-serving worker -> worker stalls -> 43s tail latencies -> k6's fixed maxVUs=150 pool exhausts -> 2329 dropped iterations -> run RED. Deterministic at rep3 because that's when cumulative span volume crosses Badger's cache threshold. The median stays 5.7-6ms throughout (app is fine); only the tail explodes. Proven by the APISIX error log timestamps aligning exactly with the rep3 window.
resolution: FIX (rig/methodology, pre-publish): the APISIX otel sampler must be FRACTIONAL, not always_on. ADR-0021 6 only needs ~500 traces per scenario for the amplification analysis, not 100% of tens of thousands. Options: (a) set opentelemetry sampler to trace_id_ratio_based / parent_based with a small fraction (e.g. 0.02-0.05) in init-routes.sh so span volume stays bounded and Badger never saturates; (b) OR raise Jaeger Badger block-cache / use the memory store for perf runs; (c) OR make the APISIX otel export non-blocking / shorter timeout so a collector stall can't stall the worker. (a) is the cleanest and matches the ADR's ~500-trace intent. SECONDARY harness robustness (already suspected): the gate-overhead/list scenarios use k6 constant-arrival-rate with a fixed maxVUs=150; a single multi-second infra stall exhausts the pool and sheds iterations, RED-ing an otherwise-valid multi-rep run — raise maxVUs and/or isolate each rep as its own scenario (the ladder-stage validity split, already applied to the ceiling ladder in SB4-port T7 but not the gate/delta multi-rep loop). VALIDLY ESTABLISHED regardless: guarded gate-overhead @ 50rps p50~=5.7ms, p90~=7ms, p99~=9-11ms, 0% fail — 9 clean measurements across 3 runs (warmup+rep1+rep2 each), tightly reproducible; this is the recordable 'ABAC gate cost' figure. NOT captured (every run died before reaching them): the two-pass ENABLE_OPA=0 unguarded baseline (so the guarded-minus-unguarded delta), list-filter/enrichment/multi-root call counts, and the ceiling ladder.

name: Scoped-identity page measurement: reset EVERY grant path of the identity + pin sample floor vs fetch cap
description: A load scenario whose measurement subject is 'the page is EXACTLY the M seeded rows for the reserved identity' (7.3 multi-root catalogs list) must (1) self-reset every OTHER grant path of that identity, not just its own fixture range — a leftover sibling-mode team (the 7.2 load team, kept by KEEP_FIXTURES=1 or a mid-run red) adds a foreign row and silently changes the per-request resolve count; enforce with a seed-time list canary asserting count==M exactly, plus wipe-first resets scoped by an unambiguous id range key (dd0 — chosen so LIKE can never match the sibling fixture ids). (2) amplification.py's chunked Jaeger fetch caps at ~300 traces (30 slices x limit 10) while the floor formula (offered/2 capped 500) can demand more: pick DURATION*REPS so floor <= ~300 or the attribution reds on arithmetic, not data (official multi-root baseline: RATE=5 DURATION=30 REPS=3 -> floor 225, 290 attributed). Baseline idiom: pin the ADR TARGET bound and let the pre-change run record the EXCEEDED finding as the honest 'before' artifact (the 7.2 2/22/102 idiom); multi-root 'before' = 51 resolves per 50-row page, median==max.
